title_en: You can get paid maternity leave
law: Code on Social Security, 2020, Chapter VI (Sections 60, 67 and 68), which replaced the Maternity Benefit Act, 1961
rule_plain: A woman worker gets paid maternity leave at her average daily wage. She must have worked at least 80 days for that employer in the 12 months before the expected delivery. She can get up to 26 weeks, with not more than 8 weeks before delivery. If she already has two or more children, she gets up to 12 weeks.
what_you_can_do: Tell your employer about your leave. Your employer must pay you for the leave.
Your employer cannot sack you during or because of your maternity leave.
If your workplace has 50 or more workers, it must have a creche, and you can visit it four times a day.
If you are not paid or are sacked, complain to the Inspector-cum-Facilitator (labour inspector).
where_to_get_help: Inspector-cum-Facilitator (labour inspector) of the Labour Department.
